explain.say: Here is a question many adults get wrong: has extreme poverty in the world gone up or down since 1990? Most people guess up. Look at the graph. Time runs along the bottom; up the side is the share of the world living in extreme poverty, which means on just a few dollars a day.

faq.a: Yes, over the long run. The share of people in extreme poverty fell from about 4 in 10 in 1990 to about 1 in 10 today, though progress slowed after 2020 and the 2030 goal is unlikely to be met.

faq.q: How many people were in extreme poverty in 1990?
faq.a: Using the World Bank's earlier 2.15-dollar line, about 38 percent of the world, roughly 2 billion people, lived in extreme poverty in 1990.

faq.q: Why did poverty fall so fast in Asia?
faq.a: Countries like China, India, Indonesia and Vietnam grew quickly, with new jobs in factories, services and farms, plus more schooling and better health care. China alone lifted hundreds of millions out of extreme poverty.
asks: Tell me about fast fall in Asia

faq.q: What happened to poverty during COVID-19?
faq.a: In 2020, lockdowns and job losses pushed tens of millions of people back into extreme poverty. It was the first rise in global extreme poverty in more than 20 years.

faq.q: How many people live in extreme poverty today?
faq.a: About 1 in 10 people, roughly 800 million, live below the World Bank's 3-dollar-a-day line, most of them in sub-Saharan Africa and in places affected by conflict.
asks: Tell me about today: about 1 in 10

facts: Ending extreme poverty everywhere by 2030 is the first of the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals, agreed in 2015.
The World Bank says 2020 saw the first increase in global extreme poverty in about a generation, due to COVID-19.

quiz.say: Since 1990, the share of the world in extreme poverty has…
quiz.why: It fell from about 4 in 10 people to about 1 in 10.

wrong.0: Many people guess this, but the data show a big fall.
wrong.1: The graph shows a steep fall, not a flat line.

quiz.say: What caused the bump in the line in 2020?
quiz.why: Lockdowns and job losses during COVID-19 pushed many people back into poverty.

wrong.1: The Olympics did not cause global poverty to rise.
wrong.2: The bump came from real job losses, not a change in how it is measured.
